### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A01 was not observed at all (0 of 200 traces); in the later window it occurs exactly once in every trace (200 of 200, mean 1.0 occurrence per trace, no repetitions), always at the same relative event position (0.5 on the position scale, with no variation). [OCC001, POS001]
- A05 shows the mirror image: it occurred exactly once in every earlier trace (200 of 200) at relative event position 0.5 with no variation, and in the later window it is not observed in any trace (0 of 200). [OCC002, POS002]
- The connections moved from A05 to A01. Earlier, A05 always led to A03; in the later window A01 always leads to A03. Earlier, A02 led to A05 in about 72 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (and to A06 in about 28 of 100); in the later window A02 leads to A01 in about 75 of 100 (A06 about 25). A07 led to A05 in about 71 of 100 earlier and leads to A01 in about 66 of 100 later; A06 led to A05 in about 29 of 100 earlier and leads to A01 in about 30 of 100 later. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Each relation A05 had re-appears as a relation of A01. Earlier, A06 always ran before A05, A05 always ran before A03, A02 preceded A05 in the 47% of traces containing A02, and A07 preceded A05 in the 53% containing A07; in the later window A06 always runs before A01, A01 always runs before A03, and A02 and A07 each precede A01 in the half of traces in which they occur (50% each). A01 and A05 never occur in the same trace in either window. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- The surrounding structure is essentially unchanged: A06 and A03 still appear in all traces in both windows, A02 (47% to 50% of traces) and A07 (53% to 50%) remain optional, and the transitions A02→A06 (about 28 to 25 in 100) and A07→A06 (about 29 to 34 in 100) remain present with similar shares. [DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 has taken over the role previously played by A05: in the later window A01 occurs once in every trace at the relative event position A05 held, is preceded by the same activities (A02, A06 and A07, with transition shares of about 75, 30 and 66 in 100 versus about 72, 29 and 71 earlier) and is followed by A03, while A05 is no longer observed. The support is direct and consistent rather than scattered: participation flips from 0 to 200 and from 200 to 0 out of 200 traces, the position profiles of A01 later and A05 earlier are identical (mean 0.5, no variation), and every relation A05 had re-appears for A01 while A01 and A05 never co-occur. Eighteen control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.13 expected if nothing had changed, so the pattern as a whole is far beyond what random re-splits of a stable process produce. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that A05 still occurs but was not sampled in the later window — zero participation strictly means only non-observation — and the logs cannot show whether A01 is a genuinely new activity or A05 recorded under a different code. [OCC002, REL003]

Other differences: within A06's outgoing transitions, the shares towards A02 and A07 swapped slightly (about 34% and 38% earlier versus 38% and 33% later); the evidence cannot establish whether this small flip is part of the same underlying difference or a separate sampling effect. [DIR004]
